original_question: A strong edge coloring assigns colors to the edges of a graph so that any two edges that are adjacent or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph. Let chi'_s(G) denote the smallest number of colors in such a coloring. Diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs can be obtained from cubic graphs by truncation, meaning that each vertex is replaced by a triangle, and T(G) denotes the cubic graph obtained by truncating a cubic graph G. Is every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph strongly 6-edge-colorable? Equivalently, is chi'_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1, "Strong edge coloring of claw-free cubic graphs".
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper very closely. It has the right notion of strong edge coloring and strong chromatic index, the right graph class (diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs), the truncation notation T(G), and the paper’s own equivalent reformulation in terms of truncations of cubic graphs. It also stays narrowly on the exact open problem posed in the paper rather than drifting to the broader claw-free subcubic setting.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, it should explicitly say that "strongly 6-edge-colorable" means admitting a strong edge-coloring with at most 6 colors.
The truncation notation T(G) should be defined explicitly inside the question as the graph obtained by replacing each vertex of a cubic graph G by a triangle.
If complete stand-alone phrasing is desired, the graph-class labels should be unpacked: claw-free means no induced K_{1,3}, and diamond-free means no induced K_4-e.

The paper’s main formulation is about diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs; the universal quantifier "for every cubic graph G" belongs to the equivalent truncation formulation and should be presented as such, not as a broader neighboring problem.
refined_question: Does every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph H admit a strong edge-coloring with 6 colors, where a strong edge-coloring is an edge-coloring in which any two edges that are adjacent or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if T(G) denotes the graph obtained from a cubic graph G by truncation (replacing each vertex of G by a triangle), is chi'_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?
justification: This is exactly the open problem posed in Section 4 as Problem 4.1. The surrounding text first defines strong edge-coloring and the strong chromatic index, then recalls the earlier 8-color and 7-color bounds for claw-free subcubic graphs and notes that the known sharp 7-color examples all contain diamonds, and only then specializes to diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs via truncation. Your draft already includes essentially all of that content, so only small stand-alone clarifications are needed.
